subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: During electrolysis of molten lead bromide, what forms at the anode?
questions.explain: The non-metal bromine is discharged at the positive anode in a molten ionic compound.

questions.q: At the anode during electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride, the product is:
questions.explain: When a halide ion is present, the halogen (chlorine) is produced at the anode rather than oxygen.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of dilute sulfuric acid, what forms at the cathode?
questions.explain: Hydrogen ions are discharged at the cathode, producing hydrogen gas.

questions.q: At the anode, what happens to negative ions?
questions.explain: Negative ions lose electrons at the anode, which is oxidation.

questions.q: Why must aluminium oxide be molten during the extraction of aluminium?
options: So the ions are free to move and carry charge
questions.explain: The aluminium oxide must be molten so its ions can move and be electrolysed.

questions.q: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than by reduction with carbon?
options: Carbon does not exist in nature
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
questions.explain: Aluminium is too reactive to be displaced by carbon, so electrolysis is required.

questions.q: For an ionic compound to act as an electrolyte it must be:
questions.explain: Ions must be free to move, which only happens when the ionic compound is molten or in solution.

questions.q: Negative ions (anions) are attracted to which electrode?
questions.explain: Anions are negative and move towards the positive anode.

questions.q: What is electrolysis?
questions.explain: Electrolysis uses an electric current to break down (decompose) a compound.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of an aqueous solution of sodium chloride, what is produced at the cathode?
questions.explain: Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen, so hydrogen is produced at the cathode instead of the metal.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of an aqueous solution containing no halide ions, what is produced at the anode?
questions.explain: With no halide present, oxygen is produced at the anode from hydroxide/water.

questions.q: During electrolysis of molten lead bromide, what forms at the cathode?
questions.explain: The metal lead is discharged at the negative cathode in a molten ionic compound.

questions.q: Which half equation shows oxidation at the anode for chloride ions?
questions.explain: Chloride ions lose electrons to form chlorine gas: 2Cl- -> Cl2 + 2e- (oxidation).

questions.q: Why can molten ionic compounds conduct electricity but solid ones cannot?
options: The ions become atoms when melted
Melting gives the ions freedom to move and carry charge
questions.explain: Melting frees the ions from the lattice so they can move and carry the current.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of aqueous potassium iodide, which product forms at the anode?
questions.explain: Because a halide (iodide) ion is present, the halogen iodine is produced at the anode.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of aqueous sodium sulfate, what forms at the cathode?
questions.explain: Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen, so hydrogen is discharged at the cathode.

questions.q: Which half equation correctly represents what happens at the cathode for copper ions?
questions.explain: At the cathode, copper ions gain electrons (reduction): Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu.

questions.q: For the electrolysis of aqueous copper sulfate, what forms at the cathode?
questions.explain: Copper is less reactive than hydrogen, so copper metal is deposited at the cathode.

questions.q: Why do solid ionic compounds not conduct electricity?
options: The ions are held in fixed positions and cannot move
questions.explain: In a solid the ions are locked in the lattice and cannot move to carry charge.

questions.q: In electrolysis, what is the charge on the cathode?
questions.explain: The cathode is the negative electrode.

questions.q: An electrolyte is a substance that:
options: Conducts electricity when molten or in solution because it contains free ions
questions.explain: An electrolyte contains ions that are free to move and carry charge when molten or dissolved.

questions.q: Which electrode do positive ions (cations) move towards?
questions.explain: Cations are positive and are attracted to the negative cathode.
